rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahr derives from notoriety or manifestation, as when someone draws and displays his sword.
rows.anchor: أما الشهر فمأخوذ من الشهرة , ومنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some linguists derive Ramadan from the severe heat that made young camels' feet burn; its naming is compared with Dhu al-Hijjah.
rows.anchor: وأما رمضان فإن بعض أهل اللغة يزعم أنه سمي بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan was called Natiq in pre-Islamic Arabia.
rows.anchor: وقد كان شهر رمضان يسمى في الجاهلية ناتقا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid disliked saying Ramadan, perhaps because he thought it might be one of God's names.
rows.anchor: وأما مجاهد فإنه كان يكره أن يقال رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the whole Quran descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on a Night of Decree in Ramadan, then was sent to the Prophet as God willed.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ إلى سماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet dates the scriptures: Abraham's scrolls on Ramadan's first night, Torah after six nights, Gospel after thirteen, and Quran after twenty-four.
rows.anchor: روى أبو مسلم عن وائلة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the Quran's descent in Ramadan as its revelation in connection with the obligation to fast Ramadan.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه بمعنى أنزل القرآن في فرض صيامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā means guidance or right direction for people.
rows.anchor: هدى للناس } يعني رشادا للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear signs explain lawful and unlawful matters, and the Criterion distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي بينات من الحلال والحرام , وفرقان بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: علي، ابن عباس، السدي
rows.claim: One view requires a resident who witnesses the month's beginning to fast through its end and forbids breaking the remaining fast.
rows.anchor: أحدها : فمن شهد أول الشهر , وهو مقيم فعليه صيامه إلى آخره

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب، الحسن البصري
rows.claim: A second view requires fasting only the part of the month witnessed while resident, not the part spent away traveling.
rows.anchor: والثاني : فمن شهد منكم الشهر , فليصم ما شهد منه وهو مقيم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وصاحباه
rows.claim: A third view reads witnessing as being adult, sane, and legally responsible; becoming insane during the month does not cancel the duty for its remainder.
rows.anchor: والثالث : فمن شهد بالغا عاقلا مكلفا فليصمه , ولا يسقط صوم بقيته

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ فَعِدَّةٌۭ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The illness and travel concession is restated because its earlier mention belonged to an abrogated ruling; anyone who breaks the Ramadan fast for either reason must make up those days afterward.
rows.anchor: وإنما أعاد ذكر الفطر بالمرض والسفر مع قرب ذكره من قبل , لأنه في حكم تلك الآية منسوخا

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri allows breaking the fast for any illness that prevents the person from praying while standing.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه كل مرض لم يطق الصلاة معه قائما , وهذا قول الحسن البصري

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i allows it when fasting is expected to worsen the illness by an intolerable amount.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه المرض الذي الأغلب من أمر صاحبه بالصوم الزيادة في علته

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin allows the concession for any condition that is called an illness.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أنه كل مرض انطلق عليه اسم المرض , وهو قول ابن سيرين

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Dawud counts any journey, short or long, as travel for this concession.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه ما انطلق اسم السفر من طويل أو قصير , وهذا قول داود

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa defines the relevant journey as a three-day journey.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه مسيرة ثلاثة أيام , وهو قول أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that breaking the fast while traveling is obligatory.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه واجب وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that breaking the fast while traveling is permitted rather than required.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه مباح , وهو قول الجمهور

words: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ease as breaking the fast and hardship as fasting while traveling; Mujahid and Qatada give a similar explanation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : اليسر الإفطار , والعسر الصيام في السفر , ونحوه عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the count means making up the days missed from Ramadan by fasting them later.
rows.anchor: يعني عدة ما أفطر ثم في صيام شهر رمضان بالقضاء في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the command as the takbir of breaking the fast, beginning with the start of the month.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه تكبير الفطر من أول الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the guidance is that it means guidance to the fast of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: على ما هداكم } يعني من صيام شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māwardī also allows the phrase to refer generally to all the religion to which God guided people.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون على عموم ما هدانا إليه من دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible object of gratitude is God's guidance.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : تشكرون على هدايته لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other possible object of gratitude is the blessing of the reward granted for obedience.
rows.anchor: والثاني : على ما أنعم به من ثواب طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manāsik means acts of worship or ritual observances; here it has two reported interpretations.
rows.anchor: أما المناسك , فهي المتعبدات , وفيها ها هنا تأويلان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes the rites completed as the sacrificial animals.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنها الذبائح , وهذا قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri takes the rites as all the acts commanded during pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: والثاني : ما أمروا بفعله في الحج , وهذا قول الحسن البصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of remembering God is saying the takbir on the days of Mina.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن هذا الذكر هو التكبير في أيام منى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is all the prescribed supplications at the various stations of pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه جميع ما سن من الأدعية في مواطن الحج كلها

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say that after pilgrimage in pre-Islamic times people gathered at Mina to boast of their ancestors' achievements, so God commanded them to remember Him instead.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد , وقتادة . والثاني : أن معناه

rows.speaker: عطاء، الضحاك
rows.claim: Ata and Dahhak compare the remembrance to small children calling repeatedly for their parents.
rows.anchor: أن معناه , فاذكروا الله كذكركم الأبناء الصغار للآباء , إذا قالوا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says people used to ask for what their fathers had possessed, mentioning the fathers rather than God, so they were told to remember God as intensely.
rows.anchor: أبيه , فأمروا بذكر الله , كذكرهم آباءهم

words: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets good in both lives as well-being in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه الحسنة العافية في الدنيا والآخرة , وهو قول قتادة

words: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة
rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Most scholars understand the prayer as asking for blessings of this world and blessings of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنها نعم الدنيا ونعم الآخرة , وهو قول أكثر أهل العلم

words: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة
rows.speaker: الحسن، الثوري
rows.claim: Hasan and al-Thawri take worldly good as knowledge and worship, and hereafter good as Paradise.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أن الحسنة في الدنيا العلم , والعبادة , وفي الآخرة الجنة

words: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة
rows.speaker: ابن زيد، السدي
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and al-Suddi take worldly good as wealth and hereafter good as Paradise.
rows.anchor: والرابع : أن الحسنة في الدنيا المال , وفي الآخرة الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māwardī says the Companions asked Muhammad about wine and gambling, and that this was the first verse revealed on the subject.
rows.anchor: يعني يسألك أصحابك يا محمد عن الخمر والميسر وشربها , وهذه أول آية نزلت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr is anything that obscures, veils, and covers the intellect.
rows.anchor: الخمر كل ما خامر العقل فستره وغطى عليه , من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root idea is covering: khamara is to cover a vessel, and the woman's khimār is named for covering her.
rows.anchor: من قولهم خمرت الإناء إذا غطيته , ويقال هو في خمار الناس

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj's line uses al-khamr for a hidden or stealthy approach; the animal in his poem does not approach stealthily but openly with banners and troops.
rows.anchor: قال العجاج : في لامع العقبان لا يأتي الخمر يوجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir means gambling and is connected to the expression yasara lī, meaning that a thing came easily or was attainable.
rows.anchor: فأما الميسر فهو القمار من قول القائل يسر لي هذا الشيء يسرا وميسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The player with arrows was called a yāsir; the term was then applied to the gambler.
rows.anchor: فالياسر اللاعب بالقداح ثم قيل للمقامر ياسر ويسر

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet likens himself to a cheated yāsir turning the arrows, illustrating the gambling sense.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشاعر : فبت كأنني يسر غبين يقلب بعدما اختلع القداحا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read kathīr, with thāʾ, instead of kabīr, with bāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي { . . . . . كثير } بالثاء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says wine's sin is that drunkenness makes the drinker harm people, while gambling's sin is withholding what is due and acting unjustly.
rows.anchor: أن شارب الخمر يسكر فيؤذي الناس , وإثم الميسر : أن يقامر الرجل فيمنع الحق ويظلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says wine removes the drinker's reason until awareness of the Creator disappears.
rows.anchor: أن إثم الخمر زوال عقل شاربها إذا سكر حتى يغرب عنه معرفة خالقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says gambling distracts from remembrance and prayer and produces enmity and hatred, as described at 5:90.
rows.anchor: وإثم الميسر : ما فيه من الشغل عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة , ووقوع العداوة والبغضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine's benefits include its sale price and trading profit, as well as the pleasure of drinking it.
rows.anchor: فمنافع الخمر أثمانها وربح تجارتها , وما ينالونه من اللذة بشربها

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit's verse presents wine as making drinkers feel like kings and lions, illustrating its pleasure or perceived benefit.
rows.anchor: كما قال حسان بن ثابت : ونشربها فتتركنا ملوكا وأسدا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A second poet contrasts wine's imagined royal grandeur while drinking with humble possessions after sobriety.
rows.anchor: وكما قال آخر : فإذا شربت فإنني … رب الخورنق والسدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account of gambling's benefit is obtaining money without labor.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : اكتساب المال من غير كد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، السدي
rows.claim: Another account is obtaining a share of the camel gambled over and divided into ten portions among the arrow winners; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Suddi are cited for this view.
rows.anchor: والثاني : ما يصيبون من أنصباء الجزور , وذلك أنهم كانوا يتياسرون على الجزور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the comparison as applying after prohibition: the sin and benefit of both practices after prohibition are compared.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن إثمهما بعد التحريم أكبر من نفعهما بعد التحريم , وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads it as a pre-prohibition comparison: the sins caused by the practices outweighed their benefits.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن كلاهما قبل التحريم يعني الإثم الذي يحدث من أسبابهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation of al-afw is what remains after providing for one's family.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بما فضل عن الأهل , وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan takes al-afw as the moderate level of spending, neither extravagance nor parsimony.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه الوسط في النفقة ما لم يكن إسرافا أو إقتارا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further report from Ibn Abbas takes al-afw as whatever people can provide, little or much.
rows.anchor: والرابع : إن العفو أن يؤخذ منهم ما أتوا به من قليل أو كثير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One view from Mujahid takes the spending as charity given from a position of sufficiency.
rows.anchor: والخامس : أنه الصدقة عن ظهر غنى , وهو قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A second view from Mujahid takes al-afw as the obligatory charity.
rows.anchor: والسادس : أنه الصدقة المفروضة وهو مروي عن مجاهد أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this spending command was abrogated by the alms tax.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس نسخت بالزكاة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the command concerning al-afw remains in force.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد هي ثابتة

rows.speaker: قوم من أهل النظر
rows.claim: Some rationalist interpreters hold that wine was prohibited by this verse.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم من أهل النظر : حرمت الخمر بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: قتادة وأكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Qatada and most scholars hold that wine was prohibited by the verse in al-Ma'idah, 5:90.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وعليه أكثر العلماء : أنها حرمت بأية المائدة

rows.speaker: أبو القلوص زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Abu al-Qalus's report says the first verse did not end drinking: two Muslims became drunk and entered prayer speaking unintelligibly, after which 4:43 was revealed and they avoided drinking at prayer times.
rows.anchor: روى عبد الوهاب عن عوف عن أبي القلوص زيد بن علي قال : أنزل الله عز وجل في الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing Abu al-Qalus's account, a man drank, lamented those killed at Badr in verse, and the Prophet arrived alarmed; the man sought God's and the Prophet's protection and vowed never to drink again.
rows.anchor: فبلغ ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاء فزعا يجر رداءه من الفزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account concludes that the prohibition in 5:90–91 was revealed, and the people answered that they had stopped.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله في تحريمها ^ { يا أيها الذين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that people continued drinking after the first verse; at a meal hosted by Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Ali led a prayer while drunk and failed to recite al-Kafirun correctly, prompting the prayer restriction in 4:43.
rows.anchor: وروى موسى عن عمرو عن أسباط عن السدي قال : نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says that before final prohibition they drank after the dawn prayer until midday, then again after the night prayer until midnight, and woke for dawn sober.
rows.anchor: فكانت لهم حلالا يشربونها من صلاة الغداة حتى يرتفع النهار أو ينتصف

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: In al-Suddi's report, a drunken dispute at a meal hosted by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas led an Anṣari to strike Sa'd's nose with a camel jawbone; the prohibition in 5:90 was then revealed.
rows.anchor: حتى صنع سعد بن أبي وقاص طعاما ودعا ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say Muslims became anxious about combining their food and drink with orphans after warnings in 17:34 and 4:10; they separated provisions, some of which spoiled, then complained to the Prophet and this permission followed.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : لما نزلت سورة بني إسرائيل , وقوله تعالى : { ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mixing with orphans includes sharing food, drink, living quarters, a riding animal, or a servant.
rows.anchor: يعني في الطعام , والشراب , والمساكنة , وركوب الدابة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says one who associates with an orphan should be generous toward him, and should not use eating together to consume the orphan's property.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي : فمن خالط يتيما , فليوسع عليه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God knows whether a person mixing his property with an orphan's intends to improve the orphan's estate or to wrongfully damage it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد : الله يعلم حين تخلط مالك بماله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the phrase as meaning that God could have imposed severe restrictions on you.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : لشدد عليكم , وهو قول السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as meaning that God could have made whatever was taken from orphans' property ruinous.
rows.anchor: والثاني : لجعل ما أصبتم من أموال اليتامى موبقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty in sovereignty and power to impose hardship, and wise in His ordering of affairs and in not imposing that hardship.
rows.anchor: يعني عزيز في سلطانه وقدرته على الإعنات , حكيم فيما صنع من تدبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who argued with Abraham is Nimrod son of Canaan, described as the first tyrant on earth and claimant to divinity.
rows.anchor: هو النمرود بن كنعان , وهو أول من تجبر في الأرض

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the pronoun refers to Nimrod: God gave him kingship, and he then disputed about God.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : هو النمرود لما أوتي الملك حاج في الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو حذيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hudhayfa says the pronoun refers to Abraham: God gave Abraham kingship, and Nimrod argued against him.
rows.anchor: والثاني : هو إبراهيم لما آتاه الله الملك حاجه النمرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥājja can mean answering an argument with a counterargument or objecting to an argument in a way that invalidates it.
rows.anchor: وفي المحاجة وجهان محتملان : أحدهما : أنه معارضة الحجة بمثلها

words: رَبِّىَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحْىِۦ وَأُمِيتُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life by releasing and sparing someone liable to execution, and death by killing without a legally sufficient cause, matching the words while evading the different causes.
rows.anchor: يريد أنه يحيي من وجب عليه القتل بالتخلية والاستبقاء , ويميت بأن يقتل

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that Nimrod's defective reply was already evident, so the sun argument reinforced the case; the other is that Abraham chose an unconfounded proof to defeat Nimrod's sophistry.
rows.anchor: ففيه جوابان : أحدهما : أنه قد ظهر من فساد معارضته ما لم يحتج معه إلى نصرة حجته

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second answer is that Abraham chose a proof free of confusion after Nimrod muddied the earlier argument with a specious objection.
rows.anchor: والجواب الثاني : أنه لما كان في تلك الحجة إشغاب منه بما عارضها به من الشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māwardī gives two answers to why Nimrod did not demand that Abraham's Lord bring the sun from the west: God deprived him of that reply, or Nimrod feared disgrace after seeing the signs.
rows.anchor: ففيه جوابان : أحدهما : أن الله خذله بالصرف عن هذه الشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second possibility is that Nimrod saw Abraham's God could do it and feared further disgrace.
rows.anchor: والجواب الثاني : أنه علم بما رأى معه من الآيات أنه يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahita has two explanations: he was perplexed, or he was silenced and had no answer.
rows.anchor: فيه قولان : أحدهما : يعني تحير

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda explains bahita as being cut off or silenced.
rows.anchor: والثاني : معناه انقطع , وهو قول أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa on both bāʾ and hāʾ makes the king the subject: he confounded Abraham with his sophistry.
rows.anchor: وقرئ : فبهت الذي كفر بفتح الباء والهاء بمعنى أن الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not guiding wrongdoers may mean that God does not help them uphold wrongdoing, or does not save them from its punishment.
rows.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : لا يعينهم على نصرة الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoing here may refer specifically to unbelief, or generally to turning from truth toward falsehood.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل الظلم هنا وجهين : أحدهما : أنه الكفر خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The injunction to treat parents well means to charge people to care for them graciously.
rows.anchor: معناه واستوصوا بالوالدين إحسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kin are blood relatives among the people of family ties.
rows.anchor: هم قرابة النسب من ذوي الأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan is someone whose father has died before the person reaches puberty.
rows.anchor: جمع يتيم وهو من مات أبوه لم يبلغ الحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A miskin is someone overcome by the humiliation of poverty and need, and who presents himself as needy.
rows.anchor: جمع مسكين وهو الذي قد ركبه ذل الفاقة والحاجة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid take the near neighbor as a neighbor related by blood.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : بمعنى ذي القرابة والرحم وهم الذين بينك وبينهم قرابة نسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is the neighbor near in Islam.
rows.anchor: والثاني : يعني الجار ذي القربى بالإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid take the distant neighbor as one far from you in lineage and without kinship ties.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الجار البعيد في نسبه الذي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is a neighbor who is distant from you in religion and is a non-Muslim.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه المشرك البعيد في دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, junub means distant; the ritually junub person is so called because he stays away from prayer until washing.
rows.anchor: والجنب في كلام العرب هو البعيد , ومنه سمي الجنب لاعتزاله الصلاة حتى يغتسل

rows.speaker: الأعشى بن قيس بن ثعلبة
rows.claim: Al-A'sha ibn Qays ibn Tha'laba's verse uses janāba for arriving from a distance, illustrating the sense of being apart.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى بن قيس بن ثعلبة : أتيت حريثا زائرا عن جنابة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada interpret the companion by one's side as a travel companion.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه الرفيق في السفر , وهو قول ابن عباس , ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud interprets the companion by one's side as a man's wife, who is alongside him.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنها زوجة الرجل التي تكون في جنبه , وهو قول ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the phrase as someone who stays close to you hoping to benefit from you.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أنه الذي يلزمك ويصحبك رجاء نفعك , وهو قول ابن زيد

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says every person accompanying another is accountable for that companionship, even if it lasted only an hour of the day.
rows.anchor: روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( كل صاحب يصحب صاحبا مسئول عن صحابته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the best companions with God are those best to their companions, and the best neighbors are those best to their neighbors.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( خير الأصحاب عند الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، الربيع
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Rabi' interpret the son of the road as a traveler passing through.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه المسافر المجتاز مارا , وهذا قول مجاهد , وقتادة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i interprets the phrase as someone who intends to travel but lacks the money for the journey.
rows.anchor: والثاني : هو الذي يريد سفرا ولا يجد نفقة , وهذا قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the son of the road as a weak person.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أنه الضعيف , وهو قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabil means road; a traveler is called the road's son as a water bird is called the son of water.
rows.anchor: والسبيل الطريق , ثم قيل لصاحب الطريق ابن السبيل

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's image of the Pleiades above a traveler's head calls him an attached son of water, illustrating the expression.
rows.anchor: وردت اعتسافا والثريا كأنها … على قمة الرأس ابن ماء ملحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those owned by one's right hand are enslaved people.
rows.anchor: يعني المملوكين , فأضاف الملك إلى اليمين لاختصاصها بالتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ownership is attributed to the right hand because it is the means of control and disposal, like saying that one's mouth spoke or foot walked.
rows.anchor: فأضاف الملك إلى اليمين لاختصاصها بالتصرف كما يقال تكلم فوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhtāl is a person possessing khuyalāʾ, conceit or swagger.
rows.anchor: المختال : من كان ذا خيلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form is derived from the verb khāla, used for a man who acts proudly or conceitedly.
rows.anchor: مفتعل من قولك : خال الرجل يخول خيلاء

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse calls the conceited person al-khāl, a garment of the ignorant, providing poetic evidence for the word.
rows.anchor: قال العجاج : والْخال ثوب من ثياب الجهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakhūr is someone who boasts over God's servants about the blessings and abundant provision God has granted him.
rows.anchor: والفخور : المفتخر على عباد الله بما أنعم الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mithqāl derives from heaviness and denotes the amount or measure of a thing by its weight.
rows.anchor: أصل المثقال الثقل , والمثقال مقدار الشيء في الثقل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the dharra as a red insect.
rows.anchor: والذرة : قال ابن عباس هي دودة حمراء

rows.speaker: يزيد بن هارون
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Harun says it is claimed that this red insect has no weight.
rows.anchor: قال يزيد بن هارون : زعموا أن هذه الدودة الحمراء ليس لها وزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness for every community is its prophet.
rows.anchor: وشهيد كل أمة نبيها , وفي المراد بشهادته عليها قولان

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن جريج، السدي
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Suddi say each prophet testifies that he delivered the message which establishes the proof against his community.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يشهد على كل أمته بأنه بلغها ما تقوم به الحجة عليها

rows.speaker: بعض البصريين
rows.claim: Some Basran scholars say each prophet testifies about his community's deeds.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يشهد عليها بعملها , وهو قول بعض البصريين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one brought as a witness over these people is the Messenger of God, testifying concerning his community.
rows.anchor: يعني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الشهادة على أمته

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud recited the verse to the Prophet, whose eyes filled with tears.
rows.anchor: روى ابن مسعود أنه قرأ على رسول الله : { فكيف إذا جئنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the unbelievers wish to be made level with the earth, as in 78:40 where the unbeliever wishes he were dust.
rows.anchor: فيه قولان : أحدهما : أن الذين تمنوه من تسوية الأرض بهم , أن يجعلهم مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other interpretation is that they wish the earth would open so that they could disappear into its depths.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنهم تمنوا لو انفتحت لهم الأرض فصاروا في بطنها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada interpret the intoxicated as drunk from wine.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : سكارى من الخمر , وهو قول ابن عباس , وقتادة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن حبيب
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Habib reports that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf hosted food and drink for companions; they became drunk, Umar led the Maghrib prayer and recited al-Kafirun incorrectly, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن حبيب : أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف صنع طعاما وشرابا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the intoxicated as overcome by sleep rather than wine.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : وأنتم سكارى من النوم , وهو قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of sukr is blockage, like stopping the flow of water; drink-induced intoxication blocks the path of understanding.
rows.anchor: وأصل السكر : السكر , وهو سد مجرى الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that a drunk person may not be so impaired that he cannot receive a command; alternatively, the verse forbids becoming drunk while a prayer is due.
rows.anchor: ففيه جوابان : أحدهما : أنه قد يكون سكران من غير أن يخرج إلى حد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second answer is that the verse forbids exposing oneself to drunkenness when a prayer is due.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه نهي عن التعرض للسكر وعليه صلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية أبي مجلز، مجاهد، الحكم، ابن زيد
rows.claim: One interpretation permits a traveler in major ritual impurity to pray after dry ablution.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أراد سبيل المسافر إذا كان جنبا لا يصلي حتى يتيمم , وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية أبي مجلز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك وابن يسار، جابر، الحسن، الزهري، النخعي
rows.claim: A second interpretation bars a person in major ritual impurity from entering mosques except to pass through.
rows.anchor: والثاني : لا يقرب الجنب مواضع الصلاة من المساجد إلا مارا مجتازا , وهذا قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: داود بن علي
rows.claim: Dawud ibn Ali allows dry ablution for any condition called illness, whether or not water would harm the person.
rows.anchor: أحدها : ما انطلق عليه اسم المرض من مستضر بالماء وغير مستضر

rows.speaker: مالك، الشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and one view of al-Shafi'i allow it where using water would cause harm, but not for illness unaffected by water.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ما استضر فيه باستعمال الماء دون ما لم يستضر

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i's second view limits the concession to cases where using water is feared to cause death.
rows.anchor: والثالث ما خيف من استعمال الماء فيه التلف دن ما لم يخف

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Dawud counts any journey, short or long, as travel for the dry-ablution concession.
rows.anchor: أحدها : ما انطلق عليه اسم السفر من قليل وكثير

rows.speaker: مالك، الشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafi'i define travel here as a day-and-night journey or longer.
rows.anchor: والثاني : مسافة يوم وليلة فصاعدا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires a journey of three days.
rows.anchor: والثالث : مسافة ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ originally meant a low place where a person went to relieve himself; it became a euphemism for excrement and then common usage made that sense nearly literal.
rows.anchor: هو الموضع المطمئن من الأرض كان الإنسان يأتيه لحاجته , فكنى به عن الخارج مجازا
